findings.summary: K-32's hover/background half is tautological: it asserts `bgStyle !== "rgb(255, 234, 158, 0.1)"`, but getComputedStyle always serializes an alpha<1 color as `rgba(...)`, never `rgb(...)` with 4 args — that literal string can never be produced by a browser, so the assertion is unconditionally true and would still pass even if a future change leaked the selected background onto a focused-but-unselected option.  [RESOLVED] Fixed — tautological comparison replaced with two positive toHaveCSS assertions (transparent when focused-unselected, rgba(255, 234, 158, 0.05) on hover); retested 6/6 then 35/35, both exit 0.

Phase 03's own Next Steps direct promoting FR-214..FR-219 into both docs/features/F004_KudosLiveBoard/ and docs/screens/SCR004_KudosLiveBoard/, but only the features docs were touched. This UI-states row still reads 'khối Phòng ban cuộn trong hộp cao tối đa 348px' (department-only) and omits the new focus glow — now stale relative to the shipped behavior, where the scroll box is the shared default for both listboxes (FR-214) and both get the focus glow (FR-215).  [RESOLVED] Fixed — the UI-states row now records the 348px box as the shared KudosFilterMenu default for both listboxes and adds the FR-215 focus glow.

FR-215's glow is additive to the browser's native :focus-visible outline (no outline-none anywhere in this file or app/globals.css), which is what actually keeps this WCAG 2.1 AA-compliant today (2.4.7 Focus Visible / 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast) — a text-shadow glow alone would not reliably clear the 3:1 non-text-contrast bar on its own. Nothing pins this down, so a later 'polish' pass adding focus-visible:outline-none to clean up the double ring would silently regress accessibility with no test catching it.  [RESOLVED] Fixed — a comment now pins the native focus outline as load-bearing for WCAG 2.1 AA and warns against adding focus-visible:outline-none.
